name: Kosmische / Berlin School
def: The synthesizer-and-tape wing of German experimental music — long, beatless or sequencer-driven pieces built from organ drones, analogue synths and tape loops. 'Kosmische Musik' began as a label marketing term; 'Berlin School' names the Tangerine Dream and Klaus Schulze sequencer style.

traits.v: Modular and analogue synths, organ, Mellotron, tape loops and delay.
Side-long pieces that evolve slowly, with or without a pulse.
From beatless drift to hypnotic step-sequencer ostinatos.

why: It takes the electronic studio's synthesis and tape methods out of the academy and into long-form rock-album listening, setting up ambient, new age and trance sequencing.

tracks.why: Its looping Moog sequence became the Berlin School template.

name: Computer Music
def: Music synthesized or composed by digital computer — from Max Mathews' MUSIC programs at Bell Labs (1957) to Koenig's algorithmic composition software at Utrecht and Chowning's FM synthesis at Stanford.

traits.v: Sound computed sample by sample, or scores generated by algorithm.
Rule-based, stochastic and serial procedures coded as software.
University and corporate research labs: Bell Labs, Utrecht, Stanford, IRCAM.

why: It moves the electronic studio's oscillators and serial procedures into code, so both the sound and the structure of a piece can be calculated.

tracks.why: The 1961 Bell Labs computer-sung version — the first widely heard demonstration of computer speech and synthesis.

name: Proto-House
def: The transitional Chicago sound — DJs splicing disco, drum machines and edits at clubs like the Warehouse, before 'house' had a name.

traits.v: Disco edits driven by drum machines.
Hypnotic, machine-locked 4/4 loop.
Early-80s Chicago club DJ culture.

why: It rebuilds disco from drum-machine edits, the missing link between the dancefloor and house.

tracks.why: Its hypnotic synth-bass loop marks the exact bridge from disco to house.

name: House
def: Chicago's machine-driven dance form — the 909 kick four-on-the-floor, soulful samples and an endlessly extendable groove.

traits.v: Four-on-the-floor 909 kick with off-beat hats.
Sampled soul/disco loops and drum-machine programming.
Long, DJ-friendly, loop-based arrangement.
Dancefloor.

why: It is large-room club architecture: a steady 909 four-on-the-floor under soulful samples, built to be mixed and extended.

tracks.why: The piano-led house anthem template defined the euphoric, song-like side of house.

name: Detroit Techno
def: Techno's birthplace — Detroit's futurist fusion of funk syncopation, European synth-pop and machine soul.

traits.v: Syncopated, funk-derived 4/4 with swung hats.
Warm analog pads and sci-fi synth leads.
Afrofuturist, melancholic machine-soul.

why: Funk's syncopation is rebuilt on drum machines and warm synths into a melancholic, futurist dance music.

tracks.why: Its stabbing string sequences proved techno could be euphoric as well as cerebral.

name: Acid House
def: House mutated by the squelching, resonant TB-303 bassline — hypnotic, psychedelic and the engine of the UK rave explosion.

traits.v: Resonant, sweeping TB-303 squelch.
Hypnotic, repetitive 4/4.
UK warehouse rave culture.

why: One machine — the resonant 303 — transforms house into a hypnotic, psychedelic rave sound.

tracks.why: An accidental misuse of the 303 created a new timbre that named a whole genre.

name: Techno
def: The harder, more mechanical and hypnotic European descendant of Detroit's sound — relentless, stripped and built for big rooms.

traits.v: Driving, machine-precise 4/4 with minimal swing.
Metallic, industrial synth and percussion.
Long, hypnotic, tool-like arrangements.
Dancefloor, peak-time.

why: It strips Detroit's soul toward relentless, metallic repetition engineered for large, dark dancefloors.

name: Deep House
def: House's introspective, jazz- and soul-infused branch — warm chords, subdued tempos and a focus on mood over peak-time impact.

traits.v: Lush jazz seventh and ninth chords.
Subdued, swung 4/4 with deep sub-bass.
Intimate, soulful after-hours rooms.

why: It turns house inward, swapping peak-time energy for warm jazz chords and a subdued, soulful mood.

tracks.why: Larry Heard's warm pad chords set the blueprint for deep house's emotional warmth.

name: Trance
def: Hypnotic, melodic electronic dance built on arpeggiated synth lines and long, euphoric builds toward a drop.

traits.v: Arpeggiated, sequenced synth motifs.
Long build, breakdown and euphoric release.
Bright major-key, emotive chord swells.
Dancefloor, peak-time euphoria.

why: Sequenced arpeggios and long breakdown-and-build arrangements engineer a sustained, euphoric emotional climb.

name: Hypnotic Trance
def: A raw, stripped revival of early-90s trance — hypnotic acid lines and hard kicks over euphoric melody, born in underground hard-dance scenes.

traits.v: Hard, fast 4/4 with rolling kicks.
Raw 303 acid lines and rugged analog leads.
Hypnotic, hands-in-the-air rave revivalism.
Dancefloor, peak-time.

why: It strips trance back to raw acid lines and hard kicks, reviving early-rave intensity over polished melody.

name: Tech House
def: The pragmatic fusion of house's groove with techno's stripped, hypnotic precision — DJ-functional, percussive and minimal.

traits.v: Percussive, minimal, swung 4/4.
Stripped, dry, functional sound design.
DJ-functional dancefloor tool.

why: It keeps house's groove as a backbone while borrowing techno's stripped, hypnotic restraint.

tracks.why: Its cuíca-driven minimal groove epitomised tech house’s playful functionality.

name: Progressive House
def: House built for the long journey — gradually evolving arrangements, layered builds and emotional, melodic peaks across extended tracks.

traits.v: Long builds and layered, evolving arrangements.
Emotive, gradually unveiled lead motifs.
Dancefloor, journey-oriented sets.

why: It extends house into long, evolving, journey-like arrangements with slow-burning melodic peaks.

name: UK Garage
def: A swung, bass-heavy UK take on house — chopped soulful vocals, skippy syncopated drums and sub-bass weight.

traits.v: Swung, syncopated 4/4 with skippy hi-hats.
Chopped, pitched soul-diva vocals; deep sub-bass.
UK pirate radio and club culture.

why: It swings house's straight 4/4 and chops soulful vocals over heavy sub-bass for a uniquely UK bounce.

name: 2-Step
def: UK garage's broken-beat mutation — a skipping, syncopated kick pattern that drops four-on-the-floor for a stuttering shuffle.

traits.v: Broken, syncopated two-step kick; no straight 4/4.
Sub-bass, clipped vocal cuts, crisp percussion.
Late-90s UK garage clubs.

why: Removing the steady four-on-the-floor for a skipping kick gives a stuttering, swung momentum that later seeds dubstep and grime.

name: IDM
def: Intelligent electronica for home listening — complex, glitchy programming and abstract melody descended from techno but aimed at the head, not the floor.

traits.v: Intricate, broken, glitch-edited programming.
Abstract, often wistful synth melody.
Listening, not dancefloor.
Detailed, sound-design-forward.

why: Techno's machine rhythm is fractured into intricate glitch programming and paired with melody made for headphones rather than clubs.

albums.t: Music Has the Right to Children

tempoNote: Range is nearly meaningless — glitch-edited programming resists a steady grid.

name: Ambient Techno
def: Techno's pulse softened into atmosphere — beats present but gentle, wrapped in ambient pads and deep space.

traits.v: Subdued, steady techno pulse at low intensity.
Lush pads, dub delay, deep reverb.
Listening and chill-room.

why: It keeps techno's steady pulse but submerges it in ambient pads and dub space for a beat-led atmosphere.
tempoNote: Variable — often drifts toward beatless passages.

name: Melodic Techno
def: A contemporary, emotive strain of techno and house with cinematic, arpeggiated melody and long, hypnotic builds.

traits.v: Arpeggiated, minor-key cinematic motifs.
Long, hypnotic builds and breakdowns.
Lush analog pads over warm, driving percussion.
Dancefloor, festival.

why: It fuses trance's emotive arpeggios with techno's drive into long, cinematic, festival-scaled builds.

name: Italo Disco
def: Disco rebuilt in Italian studios on synthesizers and drum machines — arpeggiated octave basslines, big melodic choruses sung in accented English, and a cheap, glossy, futurist romance.

traits.v: Four-on-the-floor drum machine at 115–125 BPM, hand-clap on the backbeat.
Sequenced octave synth bass, Juno and Jupiter pads, vocoder — no orchestra, no band.
Sentimental, melodic choruses, often in phonetic English.
Milan studios, the ZYX and Discomagic labels, the Rimini riviera clubs.

why: When disco's budgets vanished, Italian producers replaced the orchestra with a synthesizer and kept the chorus — Moroder's machine template made cheap, melodic and exportable.

tracks.why: The 1982 Milan record Chicago DJs looped — the clearest single link from Italo to house.

name: Synthwave
def: A retro-futurist revival of 80s film-score and synth-pop sounds — analog arpeggios, gated-reverb drums and neon nostalgia born on internet blogs.

traits.v: Analog polysynth arpeggios and gated-reverb drums.
Cinematic, minor-key 80s-soundtrack motifs.
Blog- and Bandcamp-native retro-futurism.

why: It rebuilds the imagined 1980s — synth-pop timbres and film-score arpeggios — as a nostalgic internet genre.

tracks.why: Drive's opening credits carried synthwave from blogs into the mainstream.

name: Electropop
def: Chart pop rebuilt on synth-pop's machines for the digital era — buzzing sawtooth synths, quantised drum programming and big diva hooks, from MySpace-era revivalists to festival main stages.

traits.v: Buzzing analogue-modelled synths and programmed drums.
Big, front-loaded pop hooks over machine pulse.
Loud, compressed, digital-DAW gloss.
Blog-pop and MySpace era into 2010s chart pop.

why: It carries synth-pop's all-electronic template into 21st-century chart pop — harder synths, louder production, the same hook-first machine music.

tracks.why: The sad-banger blueprint — heartbreak lyrics over relentless electropop pulse.

name: Hauntology
def: Electronic music built from the ghosts of old media — library records, public-information films, radiophonic tape and crackle — evoking futures that never arrived. Its rural strain, the 'haunted pastoral', overlays eerie English folklore onto the countryside.

traits.v: Degraded samples, tape wow, vinyl crackle and radiophonic synthesis.
Faded library-music strings, wobbling analogue tone, surface noise as instrument.
2000s UK labels (Ghost Box) and theory-blog culture; Mark Fisher named it.
Loop-based, drifting, more séance than song.

why: It turns musique concrète's tape methods and ambient's stasis toward memory itself — nostalgia for a lost future as the organising idea.

albums.t: An Empty Bliss Beyond This World
Broadcast and the Focus Group Investigate Witch Cults of the Radio Age

tracks.t: All You're Going to Want to Do Is Get Back There
tracks.why: A decaying ballroom 78 looped into pure memory-fog — hauntology in one gesture.

name: Hyperpop
def: A maximalist, internet-native pop mutation — pitched-up vocals, distorted 808s and bubblegum melody pushed to glossy, overloaded extremes.

traits.v: Auto-tuned, pitched-up, gender-fluid vocals.
Distorted 808s, saw-synth stabs, clipped maximalism.
PC Music, SoundCloud and online youth culture.

why: It fractures contemporary pop and R&B through IDM-grade sound design into a deliberately overloaded, digital-native maximalism.

tracks.why: Its cartoonish pitch-shifting and blown-out bass define hyperpop excess.

tempoNote: Highly variable — maximalist songs jump tempo mid-track.

name: Electroclash
def: Trashy analogue synths, deadpan vocals and fashion-world sleaze — new wave and electro revived as knowing, confrontational club music.

traits.v: Cheap-on-purpose analogue synths and drum machines.
Spoken, bored, heavily accented cool.
Berlin–New York club and fashion underground, c. 2001.

why: It weaponised 80s synth kitsch as attitude — proving revival could be a provocation, not nostalgia.

tracks.why: Bored, spoken decadence over a cheap electro thump — the genre’s manifesto.

name: French Touch
def: Parisian house built from filtered disco loops — compressed, phase-swept samples turned into euphoric, endlessly cresting grooves.

traits.v: Filter sweeps and sidechain pump on looped disco samples.
Steady house four with disco’s bounce intact.
Warm, compressed, vinyl-sourced glow.

why: It made the filter itself the hook — one disco bar, opened and closed, generates the whole arrangement.

tracks.why: A g-funk squelch filtered into house — the French Touch blueprint.

name: Eurodance
def: Mid-90s European club-pop — a 130–150 BPM four-on-the-floor kick, rave synth stabs, a rapped male verse and a belted female chorus. House and hi-NRG rebuilt as radio song.

traits.v: Rap verse / diva chorus at 130–150 BPM; radio-length.
Bright rave stabs, hoover leads, sequenced octave bass.
Male rapper against a soaring female hook.
German, Dutch, Belgian and Italian studios; MTV Europe and Eurochart.

why: It compresses house and rave into a pop song — rap verse, diva chorus, synth hook — and sells the club to the charts.

tracks.why: The template: hoover riff, rap verse, chanted chorus, nothing wasted.

name: Hands Up
def: Eurodance sped up and fed through trance — supersaw leads, pitched-up female vocals and a hard, bouncy kick, the sound of 2000s European teen clubs and ringtone charts.

traits.v: Hard, bouncy 4/4 at 140–150 BPM with off-beat bass.
Supersaw leads, pitched-up vocal, sidechained pads.
Trance build and breakdown inside a three-minute pop form.
German and Scandinavian dance charts, Hamburg and Cologne studios.

why: It grafts trance's supersaw lead and breakdown onto the Eurodance pop chassis, faster and harder.

tracks.why: The definitive Hands Up single — a ballad rebuilt as a 142 BPM supersaw anthem.

name: Hardstyle
def: Dutch hard dance — a distorted, pitched reverse-bass kick at 150 BPM, euphoric trance melodies in the breakdown and a stadium-rave scale that now fills Defqon.1 and Tomorrowland.

traits.v: Reverse-bass kick at 150 BPM; kick and bass fused into one pitched hit.
Distorted, saturated kick; screeching leads; wide euphoric pads.
Melodic climax breakdown, then the kick returns.
Dutch festival culture — Q-dance, Defqon.1, Qlimax.

why: It fuses kick and bass into one pitched, distorted hit and pairs it with trance-scale euphoria, hardcore's power with Hands Up's melody.

tracks.why: Cinematic breakdown into reverse-bass kick — the modern euphoric hardstyle blueprint.

name: Y2K Dance-Pop Revival
def: Eurodance and Hands Up returning as chart pop — sampled or re-sung 90s club hooks, 128 BPM four-on-the-floor and glossy modern production, spread by TikTok and festival main stages.

traits.v: Modern loud-pop mix over a 90s Euro hook, often a direct sample or rework.
Steady 125–130 BPM four-on-the-floor with slap-house bass.
Big, nostalgic 90s synth riffs and chanted choruses.
TikTok, Ibiza main rooms, European pop radio.

why: It lifts Eurodance's hooks intact and re-cuts them at pop tempo with contemporary loudness, nostalgia as club currency.

tracks.why: A near-literal rework of Eiffel 65's 'Blue' — the revival's flagship.

name: Jersey Club
def: Newark’s chopped, 130+ BPM club style — stuttering kick triplets, bed-squeak samples and vocal chops — now rewiring mainstream rap and pop.

traits.v: Signature 5-kick triplet bounce at 130–140 BPM.
Chopped vocal stabs and cheeky found-sound samples.
From Newark parties to drill, K-pop and TikTok ubiquity.

why: Its kick pattern is currently pop’s favourite rhythmic transplant — the clearest case of a regional club style colonising the mainstream.

tracks.why: The TikTok moment that carried Jersey club’s bounce worldwide.
